newsitem.title: JAPAN: S.Africa's Manuel says not worried about rand fall.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Manuel says not worried about rand fall.

text.p: South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Wednesday he was not worried about the recent fall in the rand's value, triggered by worries over the country's planned relaxation of exchange controls on July 1.
Manuel, on a four-day visit to Japan, told a news conference: "The sky has not fallen because there has been a little bit of movement of the rand... We're not concerned about the movement."

The rand has come under pressure due to worries over a possible flight of capital after exchange controls on individuals are eased on July 1, allowing South Africans to invest in offshore markets for the first time.

Asked about the size of the possible outflow of individual capital, Manuel said: "Your guess is as good as mine... Chances are that there are a number of South Africans who already have wealth abroad. It's hard to speculate."
South Africa plans to lift foreign exchange controls on ordinary South Africans on July 1, although a limit will be placed on the amount they can invest overseas.
Although the figure has not yet been set, Manuel said an announcement would be made by the Reserve Bank, probably within the next few days.
